title: Development of a novel multiplex electrochemiluminescent-based immunoassay to aid enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli vaccine development and evaluations.
ehr_evidence: We used the serum and ALS (antibody in lymphocyte supernatant) samples from the volunteers vaccinated with ACE527 vaccine and placebo volunteers challenged with H10407 ETEC for validation of the multiplex ECL assay.
summary: Development and validation of a novel 8-plex multiplex electrochemiluminescent (ECL) immunoassay using the MSD platform to measure immune responses to ETEC antigens, compared against conventional ELISA.
key_findings: Intra-assay variability showed percent CV below 20% (range 5.3%–18.1%) for all 8 antigens.
Inter-assay variability showed percent CV below 20% (range 7.7%–17.9%) across 3 consecutive days.
Dilution linearity yielded R² values between 90% and 100% for high titer samples and 75% to 90% for low titer samples.
Specificity testing showed over 60% inhibition for all antigens.
Concordance analysis showed no significant difference between ECL and ELISA for most antigens (p < .05), except CS3 (p = .0087) and LTB IgG (p = .0200).
ECL demonstrated higher sensitivity than ELISA, with a maximum to minimum signal ratio of 1434.62 compared to 87.63 for ELISA.
captured_features: Serum IgA and IgG antibody titers
data_source_type: Biospecimens (serum and ALS from vaccine trial volunteers)
population: Healthy American adults enrolled in the ACE527 ETEC vaccine trial
limitations: High reader and plate costs compared to ELISA
Specialist printing requirements for multiplex plates
